title: The Station Terriers
logline: A retired station pest handler refuses to surrender thirty aging radiation-hunting terriers marked for euthanasia by sanitation authorities, hiring an armed pilot to defend their evacuation.

roles.description: Spent forty years clearing electrical-eating rodents from station conduits alongside his pack of terriers; scarred, fierce, protective.
Enforces biological contamination codes; treats working animals as unnecessary atmospheric consumers that should be purged.
A heavy municipal pest-control cutter equipped with chemical fumigation cannons and boarding clamps.
The administrative agency responsible for biological containment and vermin extermination across the docks.
A cold, unpressurized lower-deck kennel where working dogs sleep between maintenance shifts.
A disused orbital greenhouse on the system rim whose owners have offered a permanent home to the dogs.

public_situation: Sanitation authorities issue an emergency cull notice for working ship terriers across {system}, citing an unverified flea-borne pathogen.
private_truth: {role:sanitation_commissioner} fabricated the disease report to clear {role:pest_control_depot} and sell the valuable lower-deck real estate to a data-server firm.

beats.public_change: Sanitation marshals padlock the kennel airlocks, deploying gas cylinders to fumigate the animals.

missions.reason: He needs canine emergency oxygen hoods and medical sedatives delivered through a maintenance hatch to prepare thirty dogs for vacuum transfer.
missions.private_fact: His lead terrier saved his life twenty years ago by dragging him out of a flooded reactor conduit.

beats.public_change: The commissioner announces that any vessel attempting to carry quarantined animals will be fired upon on sight.

missions.reason: He needs the pilot to scan the sanitation bureau's bio-sensor relays and prove the dogs' blood samples test completely clean of infection.
missions.private_fact: The commissioner offered him a comfortable retirement pension if he agreed to lead the dogs to the gas chamber himself.

beats.public_change: {role:exterminator_gunboat} deploys into open flight outside the depot, powering chemical dispersal cannons to vent the kennel.

missions.reason: He needs the exterminator gunboat disabled so his transport shuttle can break mooring and reach {role:sanctuary_outpost}.
missions.private_fact: The gunboat skipper hails mid-fight offering fifty thousand credits in municipal scrip to withdraw and let the gas deployment finish.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot disables the gunboat and secures the dog transport.
resolutions.summary: The terriers reach {role:sanctuary_outpost} safely. The fabricated contamination is exposed, and {role:sanitation_commissioner} is removed from office.

consequences.public_summary: A mercenary crippled a sanitation gunboat to help an old rat-catcher save thirty working ship dogs from the gas chambers.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot accepts the sanitation bribe and lets the gas proceed.
resolutions.summary: The working dogs are destroyed. {role:sanitation_commissioner} sells the kennel to data server developers, and {role:retired_handler} is left broken and alone.

consequences.public_summary: Dockside whispers recount how a hired pilot took sanitation money to look away while thirty faithful ship dogs were euthanized.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot abandons the contract or fails the mission line.
resolutions.summary: Sanitation crews breach the kennel and administer lethal gas. The depot is cleared for server installations, and the working hounds are forgotten.

loose_threads.detail: A draft lease for {role:pest_control_depot} was signed with an offshore data-mining firm two weeks before the contamination was declared.
The municipal bio-lab blood tests on the terriers show negative pathogen markers, stored under an encrypted supervisor lock.
The gunboat's chemical cargo receipt was billed to municipal development accounts rather than veterinary quarantine reserves.

radio_hooks: Sanitation department announces mandatory bio-hazard culling for domestic vermin control packs.
Station engineers protest the loss of canine pipe-sniffers ahead of scheduled reactor refits.
Commercial server companies announce plans to expand lower-deck data processing facilities.

voice_direction.retired_handler: Raspy, choked with emotion, and fiercely protective. Speaks of his dogs with the deep, reverent loyalty normally reserved for squad mates in a trenches war.
voice_direction.sanitation_commissioner: Polished, cold, and utterly patronizing. Treats the execution of thirty faithful working animals as a routine facilities modernization exercise.
